doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Tramp bands and the Chicago Maniacs
summary: With older neighborhood boys and his homemade fiddle, Ware plays in kazoo and washtub tramp bands, hustling taverns and winning amateur contests.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And during that time, I met some neighborhood older boys -- I was going on 10, maybe 11 -- and they had little string groups, and what you would call a tramps bands, and they'd have kazoos, and a washboard -- one fellow had a tenor guitar; I

had my home made bass. One fellow had a tin tub drum -- that's a drum that sits in an old washtub and a 5 gallon oil drum that had one of the heads cut out of it -- a whole lot of holes in it; there were some nails in it, and that was your snare drum.

It was a certain way they built it that was sturdy and had at least 3 skillets nailed to the top of the tin tub, and there are some old cats that are still around who would know about that tin tub drum. But the tramp bands at that time -- were very popular. There was a tramp band at the Cotton Club; and they started traveling around with Cab Calloway in the Cotton Club Revue -- they were out of Chicago, and I think they made a movie. I think they were in "Stormy Weather", but you couldn't recognize them. But they were quite popular.

And another group that I come up with -- I had to be about 12 then -- was the Chicago Maniacs, and they were some older boys in the neighborhood that I'm speaking of, who had 3 kazoos. The fellows had these old Victrolas -- the speakers were shaped something like a saxophone, you might say, a small saxophone and a big saxophone, that was your alto and your tenor -- and the guy who played the trumpet, he'd steal one of those brass from those old Buicks; just screw it off and stick the kazoo in there, and he had a trumpet.
And like I said, we had a washboard, tenor guitar,

tenor drum, and my home made fiddle. We had a fellow named Jake who played piano. Yeah, there was a piano. And we'd go out hustling from tavern to tavern and roadhouse to roadhouse, plus we played amateur shows all around Chicago. And win. The prize was $3, and I guess we had 8 pieces, but that was a nice piece of money during that time.

We also played the Savoy Ballroom. They had a barn-dance and they had a tramp band contest. Well, the Chicago Maniacs came out on top; maybe if some old Chicagoans could remember those days ... The Riviera Theatre used to have amateur shows -- I think this was during the time; I don't know, when was the time of that first flood? Wasn't it in Pennsylvania, a big flood, and they had benefits all over the country, and they had a benefit at the Riviera Theatre. I know Les Louis Armstrong was there.

And we played. That tramp band was something. And from the tramp band, the fellows started using guitars, trios and quartets, singing some barbershop harmony, and doing tunes like "China Boy" and "Chinatown" and "Tiger Rag". And I'm still playing this home made fiddle. At the same time, I'm going to school.
